title: "Now, yoga." Yoga is the stilling of the turnings of the mind (1.1–1.2)
hook: the most famous text on yoga opens with a single small word, and defines yoga in four more
tomorrow: then the seer rests in itself

segments.voice: Yesterday we closed the Upanishads with three words: tat tvam asi, you are that. Did you think them, once, looking at someone? Today a new block begins: the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali. Day four hundred thirty.

Picture a yoga studio: mats, mirrors, someone holding a long, shaking plank. Now picture the book the whole word comes from. The Yoga Sutras are 195 short threads of Sanskrit, in the common count, collected under the name Patanjali sometime, scholars think, between a few centuries before the common era and about 400. Just three of those threads are about posture. The rest are about the mind. And the book opens with a word so small you could miss it. One word, and then a definition that has been argued over ever since.
screen: `MATS, MIRRORS, A SHAKING PLANK.` → `195 THREADS OF SANSKRIT.` → `THREE ABOUT POSTURE. THE REST: THE MIND.`

segments.voice: Sutra 1.1: atha yoga anushasanam. Now, the teaching of yoga. Atha means now, and in old Sanskrit books it marks a beginning: here the real subject starts. There's a traditional verse that says two sounds came first from the creator's throat, om and atha, so both are lucky words to begin with. Some teachers also hear a quieter meaning: now, when you are ready, after everything else has been tried. The word anushasanam is interesting too. Anu means following. This is a teaching that follows, handed down, not invented on the spot. Then sutra 1.2 gives the whole definition: yogash chitta vritti nirodhah. Yoga is the stilling of the turnings of the mind. Chitta is the mind, the whole field of thinking and feeling. Vritti means a turning, a whirl, the way water turns in an eddy. Nirodha means stopping, or holding still. So yoga, in this book, isn't a shape you make with the body. It is the moment the mind's whirling settles. Notice how plain that is. No god is named yet, no stretch, no secret. Just the mind, its movements, and the possibility that they can quiet down. The next fifty sutras are a manual for that. Where the Upanishads said you are that, Patanjali asks the practical question: then why doesn't it feel like it, and what can you do, starting now?
screen: `ATHA: NOW, THE TEACHING BEGINS.` · `ANUSHASANAM: HANDED DOWN.` · `CHITTA, VRITTI, NIRODHA.` · then, large: `YOGA IS THE STILLING OF THE TURNINGS.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably, spine upright. For a few breaths, simply watch the turnings: a thought arrives, it swirls, it goes. Don't fight them. Then, each time you notice you've been carried off, say to yourself, silently, one word: now. Atha. Not as a scolding. As a fresh start. Now, and settle back on the breath. Now, and settle again. Every return is the first sutra, said again. The bell holds the time.
"Now. The first word of the Yoga Sutras, atha: the teaching begins here, and so does the practice, every time you come back.
Your line: atha. Now. Three times today, when you notice your mind whirling, say the word silently, and let it be a fresh start rather than a correction. Day four hundred thirty.

screen: `DAY 430 COUNTS.` → `BLOCK B, THE YOGA SUTRAS, BEGINS.` → `TOMORROW: THEN THE SEER RESTS IN ITSELF.`

howItsDone: Students of yoga in many Hindu lineages begin study of the Yoga Sutras by chanting 1.1 and 1.2, often with Vyasa's classic commentary, and treat 1.2 as the definition the whole text unfolds.

myth: the Yoga Sutras are mainly about physical postures
only three sutras (2.46–2.48) deal with posture. the rest are about the mind.
the Yoga Sutras open with the word atha, now
atha yoga anushasanam: now, the teaching of yoga.
scholars agree on the exact year Patanjali wrote
estimates run from a few centuries before the common era to around 400 CE.

fork.setup: Patanjali has one sentence to define yoga. which does he choose?
options: yoga is union of body and breath.
yoga is the stilling of the turnings of the mind.
yoga is flexibility of the body.
fork.reveal: yogash chitta vritti nirodhah, sutra 1.2. yoga is the settling of the mind's whirling.

original.note: Sanskrit atha: now. the first word of the Yoga Sutras, a traditional mark of a beginning.

trapdoor: what you thought: 'now' is filler before the real start.
what it means: the teaching begins here, and the practice begins every time you come back.

what a scholar hears: Vyasa's commentary reads atha as marking the start of a subject (adhikara); a traditional verse says om and atha first came from Brahma's throat, so both are auspicious openings.

notes: Block B opens (days 430–489). Opening day of the Yoga Sutras.
Date range for the Yoga Sutras is contested; many scholars now place the compilation around 325–425 CE, older views earlier. Phrased as a range.
195 sutras is the common count (some editions 196). Asana sutras counted as three (2.46–2.48).
Traditional verse that om and atha came from Brahma's throat: commonly cited by commentators; confirm source.
The index word is '"Now' (title head with a leading quotation mark); kept exactly as the validator requires. Suggest the outline use 'atha' or 'now' as the word.
